Here's the answer.

## Where streaming is implemented

**Core SSE transport** — `src/core/streaming.ts`
- `Stream<Item>` class (line 21): wraps a `Response` body as an `AsyncIterable`. Static factory `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` (line 32) parses Server-Sent Events into typed chunks.
- `_iterSSEMessages()` (line 219) and `SSEDecoder` (line 287): low-level SSE frame parsing (splits on `\n\n`, decodes `event:`/`data:` fields), built on `LineDecoder` from `src/internal/decoders/line.ts`.

**Dispatch point** — `src/internal/parse.ts`, function `defaultParseResponse()` (~line 18): every API call funnels through here. If `props.options.stream` is true, it calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or a custom `__streamClass` if the caller supplied one) instead of parsing JSON. This is the single chokepoint where a "normal" response becomes a stream.

**Higher-level stream helpers** (build on `Stream`, add typed events/accumulation):
- `src/lib/EventStream.ts` — generic `EventStream<EventTypes>` base class (event emitter + async iterator over typed events), line 3.
- `src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream` class (line 65), for the Responses API. `_createOrRetrieveResponse()` (line 167) calls `client.responses.create({...params, stream: true}, ...)` (line 185).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts` — `ChatCompletionStream` class (line 130), for Chat Completions. Calls `client.chat.completions.create({...params, stream: true}, ...)` at line 380.
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` — extends `ChatCompletionStream` to add automatic tool-call execution while streaming.
- `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts` — `AssistantStream` class (line 73), for the (deprecated) Beta Assistants/Threads/Runs API; also extends `EventStream`.
- `src/beta/realtime/` and `src/resources/realtime/` — a separate, non-SSE streaming path over WebSocket (`websocket.ts`, `ws.ts`) for the Realtime API; not built on `core/streaming.ts`.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.responses.create(body, opts)` with `stream: true` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts` (~line 100) | passes `stream: body.stream ?? false` to `this._client.post(...)` → `defaultParseResponse` → `Stream.fromSSEResponse` |
| `client.responses.stream(body, opts)` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts` (`stream()` method, ~line 205) | calls `ResponseStream.createResponse(...)` |
| `client.chat.completions.create(body, opts)` with `stream: true` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts` (~line 65) | same `stream` flag → `Stream.fromSSEResponse` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(body, opts)` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts` (bottom of class) | calls `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion(...)` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(body, opts)` when `body.stream` truthy | same file | delegates to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create(...).stream(...)` / `.createAndPoll` streaming variants, `runs.stream()`, `runs.submitToolOutputsStream()` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` (lines ~168, 232, 297) | calls `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream` / `createToolAssistantStream` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRunStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts` (line 182) | calls `AssistantStream.createThreadAssistantStream(...)` |

Any `.create()`-style method whose params object includes a `stream: true`/`ResponseCreateParamsStreaming` overload (e.g. `responses.create`, `chat.completions.create`) ultimately returns `APIPromise<Stream<...>>`, resolved through the same `defaultParseResponse` chokepoint in `src/internal/parse.ts`.

## Not verified
- I did not read the full body of `src/lib/AssistantStream.ts`, `src/beta/realtime/*`, or `src/resources/realtime/*` line-by-line (only mapped signatures/grepped) — confirmed their entry points wire in, but didn't trace their full internal event-accumulation logic.
- Did not check `src/resources/audio/` (e.g., real-time transcription) or `src/resources/containers` for any additional streaming surfaces beyond what grep/search surfaced.
- Did not run or execute any code — this is static analysis of source read via `ghx` only.
